name: Exploratory Analysis Conventions
description: This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on exploratory analysis so output stays consistent and easy to review.
content:
This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on exploratory analysis so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Check that exploratory analysis terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
2. Keep exploratory analysis changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
3. When multiple exploratory analysis strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
4. Prefer explicit, readable exploratory analysis solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
5. Prefer the simplest exploratory analysis approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
6. Measure before optimizing any exploratory analysis bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
7. Keep exploratory analysis outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
8. When exploratory analysis decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
9. Validate exploratory analysis outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
10. Before starting exploratory analysis work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of exploratory analysis correctness.
- Do not skip documenting exploratory analysis assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid mixing unrelated exploratory analysis concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not apply generic exploratory analysis advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop exploratory analysis edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these exploratory analysis guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
